tutorials.title: Find code about a topic in everyday words
tutorials.goal: Find projects about something you care about without knowing GitHub's words.

steps.title: Type what you're looking for
steps.text: Use everyday words, such as 'benefits', 'school data' or 'maps'. The thesaurus also finds the technical words for them.

steps.title: Narrow it down
steps.text: Choose what kind of thing you want back: projects, organisations, topics, APIs, words and more.

steps.title: Read the results
steps.text: Results are grouped by kind, best match first. Select one to open it.

steps.title: How search works
steps.text: This explains how results are ranked, so you know why something came first.
steps.head: How search works

tutorials.title: Read a project's profile
tutorials.goal: Understand what a project does, who it belongs to and whether it's looked after.

steps.title: The project at the top
steps.text: Its name in plain English, with the GitHub name underneath. Listen to it with the read-aloud button if that helps.

steps.title: At a glance
steps.text: Whether it's live, how recently someone changed it and who publishes it.
steps.head: At a glance

steps.title: Who it belongs to
steps.text: The chain from the GitHub account up to the government department.
steps.head: Who it belongs to

steps.title: How well it's looked after
steps.text: A simple checklist: description, licence, recent changes, security and tests.
steps.head: How well it's looked after

steps.title: Words explained
steps.text: Any technical word on this page, explained in a sentence.
steps.head: Words explained

tutorials.title: Find who a project belongs to
tutorials.goal: Go from a department to the organisations and GitHub accounts where its code lives.

steps.title: Find an organisation
steps.text: Type a department or public body. Matches come from GOV.UK's list of organisations.

steps.title: The family tree
steps.text: Each department with the organisations under it. Open a branch to see more.

steps.title: The selected organisation
steps.text: Its GitHub accounts, its projects and how much of its code is still being worked on.

tutorials.title: Explore projects with filters
tutorials.goal: Use filters, sorting and grouping to find work you could reuse.

steps.title: Start with an interest
steps.text: Pick a topic tile to start, or skip to searching.
steps.head: 1. What are you interested in?

steps.title: Search in everyday words
steps.text: Type words; the line under the box shows which related words were also searched.

steps.title: Filter by sector
steps.text: Keep only health, education, justice or another sector. Other filters show live projects, reusable ones or those with legacy signals.

steps.title: Sort and group
steps.text: Sort by recent work, name or size, and group by sector, kind or organisation.

steps.title: The projects
steps.text: Each card says what the project is in plain English. Open one for its full profile.

tutorials.title: See patterns across the estate
tutorials.goal: Use the dashboard to answer estate-wide questions, then check the numbers behind each chart.

steps.title: Filter the whole dashboard
steps.text: Choose a sector, kind of body, topic or data management area; every chart follows.

steps.title: Growth over time
steps.text: New code projects each year, coloured by whether they are still worked on today.
steps.head: New code projects each year

steps.title: Who publishes most
steps.text: The organisations with most public code. Select a bar to open that organisation.
steps.head: Who publishes most

steps.title: Legacy at a glance
steps.text: Where legacy technology and technical debt show up. Every chart has 'Show the numbers' for a table.
steps.head: Legacy and technical debt at a glance

tutorials.title: Check good practice against the GDS Way
tutorials.goal: Judge how well code is looked after and where it falls short of the GDS Way.

steps.title: Practice across government
steps.text: Signals such as licences, security policies, tests and automated checks, by organisation.
steps.head: Engineering practice across government

steps.title: GDS Way checks
steps.text: Each co-cddo repository checked against the GDS Way, with the evidence for each result.
steps.head: GDS Way conformance

steps.title: Moving safely
steps.text: GitHub's recommended order for changes that can break things.
steps.head: GitHub's recommended approach

tutorials.title: Find legacy technology and technical debt
tutorials.goal: Locate legacy signals by organisation and sector, and export the evidence.

steps.title: The signals
steps.text: Each signal, such as retired libraries or code nobody has changed for years, with how many projects show it.
steps.head: Signals

steps.title: Filter
steps.text: Narrow by sector, organisation, live projects or the core signals only.

steps.title: The projects
steps.text: Every project with its signals and the evidence for each.

steps.title: Export
steps.text: Download the filtered list as CSV for your own analysis.

steps.title: How accurate it is
steps.text: How the signals are found and how precise they were on a checked sample.
steps.head: How the signals are found

tutorials.title: Reuse the knowledge graph and vocabularies
tutorials.goal: Find any item's connections and download the vocabularies in open formats.

steps.title: The knowledge layer
steps.text: A graph, lineage, vocabularies, an ontology, a data dictionary and a thesaurus, as tabs.

steps.title: Find an item
steps.text: Search the graph for a project, organisation, topic or requirement and see what it connects to.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Every part downloads in open formats: JSON-LD, SKOS, OWL, PROV and CSV.

tutorials.title: Join the catalogue to other apps
tutorials.goal: Use the organisation feeds and crosswalk to join this catalogue with other apps.

steps.title: How the apps join
steps.text: Every app can join on one key: the GOV.UK organisation slug.
steps.head: How this catalogue links to

steps.title: The feeds
steps.text: Download organisation and repository feeds as JSON, CSV or DCAT.

steps.title: The crosswalk
steps.text: Other apps' organisation ids matched to GOV.UK slugs, with the reason for every gap.

tutorials.title: Go from a data management activity to the tools that deliver it
tutorials.goal: Find what an activity involves, the UK guidance for it, and the tools and code that deliver it.

steps.title: Choose a knowledge area
steps.text: The eleven areas of the DAMA wheel come first, then five DMBOK2 topics beyond it. Each card shows how many activities and tools it has.

steps.title: Find the activity
steps.text: Filter by phase, lifecycle stage or whether tools deliver it, or search in your own words, such as 'lineage' or 'retention'.

steps.title: Read the activity
steps.text: What it is, its deliverables, who does it, how it is measured, the UK guidance that applies, and the tools and code that deliver it.

steps.title: See it across the data lifecycle
steps.text: How many activities act at each stage, from planning to disposal. Select a number to list them.

tutorials.title: Find out who uses a tool, for what, where and when
tutorials.goal: See the evidence that a tool is used in the public sector, and by whom.

steps.title: Find the tool
steps.text: Filter by knowledge area, activity, lifecycle stage, type, evidence or the buyer's sector, then sort by the evidence you care about.

steps.title: Read who uses it
steps.text: Case studies from the supplier's own site, tender and contract notices with buyer, date, value and supplier, public code, and G-Cloud listings.

steps.title: See who buys what
steps.text: Notices by knowledge area and the buyer's sector. Select a number to filter the tools.

steps.title: Find the buyers
steps.text: The public bodies with the most notices for these tools, and which tools they named.
